## S0071 — historical audit (visible chunk 1 of 6)

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. The reference and rendered images are not visible in the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The goal was an editable, separate-mesh reconstruction of one indoor photograph, matching viewpoint and appearance. The student received the image path and constraints, including no diagnostic probes. The particular chaise-room interpretation is the student’s inference, not independently observed here. |
| Student response, line 3 | The draft specifies separate architecture, window, chaise, pillow, card and foreground-chair assets; parquet, fabric motifs and cane are modeled as geometry and colors. It specifies a tilted headrest and pillow, camera, world and lights. Asset grouping and intended support do not prove physical contact or visual correctness. |
| Student model request, line 4 | An actual **source-audit-only user/controller instruction** says the draft had not executed and no render existed. It requests checks for dimensions, keys, World and local materials, while preserving composition. It does not identify a particular defect or supply a visual diagnosis. No separately identified teacher message is visible. |
| Student response, line 6; execute step 1, line 7 | The revision adds checked constructors and duplicate-key assertions, subtree material lookup and copies; it changes foot radius from .052 to .045 and rotates the card and printing together. These are visible adoption of the audit request, not evidence that a teacher detected a defect. The revised program was sent to Blender. |
| Execution result, line 8, characters [0,154042); select, line 9 | Step 1 reports `ok: true`, a finished render, saved PNG and blend file, followed by selection of step 1. This is a successful execution and render operation, not a formal visual, geometric or editability pass. No reference/render pixels or comparison are supplied. |

**Exploration and outcome.** Two completed student CLI sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 and 5); the source revision was prompted, not an observed autonomous diagnostic search. The student made its own initial scene and camera estimates, but no camera sweep or independent geometric validation is visible. The observed build is nonempty and execution succeeded; overall reconstruction correctness and final outcome remain **unknown**, not established algorithm failure or an empty patch.

**Uncertainty and lessons.** Multiple objects, part hierarchy, poses, material treatments, camera and lighting are evidenced in code, but their visibility, connections, occlusion, textures and match to the photograph remain unverified. In particular, the foreground chair’s intended crop and the pillow’s actual support are hypotheses, as are camera framing and lighting quality. Transferably, source assertions and isolated material copies can guard construction operations; a successful render alone cannot establish scene fidelity. The specific chaise, parquet and card design are task-specific inferences. Later chunks and any subsequent review are outside this audit.
